title: Transportability from Toronto: randomized trial and different click-through rate
content: Figure 10.2(e) removes the Age-to-Advertisement confounding edge because Toronto is a randomized trial, retains Age Z -> Purchase Y, and adds selector S -> Click-through Rate W. The source says the effect is estimable for Arkansas if X, W, and Y are measured there.

variables.name: Purchase Decision (Y)
variables.content: Whether the consumer purchases the product.

variables.name: Age (Z)
variables.content: Age, which still affects Purchase Decision.

variables.name: Click-through Rate (W)
variables.content: The mediator whose population mechanism differs.

variables.name: Population Difference (S)
variables.content: The difference-producing selector for Toronto click-through rate.

arrows.because: Figure 10.2(e) retains Age as a cause of Purchase Decision.
Advertisement causes Click-through Rate in the randomized trial.
Figure 10.2(e) points selector S to Click-through Rate W.
